intervals.label: GP300_s13
intervals.note: Quote text is from the 2026 JINST paper (arXiv:2509.21306), not the ICRC 2025 proceedings it was previously attributed to. The ICRC 2025 proceedings (arXiv:2507.05915) give different stage dates (GP13 deployed Feb 2023 to Oct 2024; 65 DUs deployed Oct 2024, all in place by June 2025); the 2026 collaboration paper is followed here.
intervals.quote: In June 2023, the deployment of the 13-antenna stage, GP300_s13, was completed ... GP300_s13 was decommissioned in April 2025

name: GRANDProto300 (GRAND prototype)
notes: No source consulted gives a numeric coordinate for the precise Gobi Desert / Dunhuang array site (only 'near Xiaodushan, in northern Dunhuang, China'); the placement above points at the nearest named city (Dunhuang) as a coarse regional pointer rather than a surveyed array position.

placements.note: Placed at the nearest named city (Dunhuang) as a coarse regional pointer only; see site:grandproto300-dunhuang for why no precise coordinate exists. Start (2023-06) is the completion of the 13-antenna stage per the 2026 JINST paper (arXiv:2509.21306), which also gives the site description.
placements.quote: will span an area of about 200 km² in the Gobi Desert near Xiaodushan, in northern Dunhuang, China ... In June 2023, the deployment of the 13-antenna stage, GP300_s13, was completed

area.note: Design target for the full GRANDProto300 stage (300 antennas) is about 200 km² (same paper).
area.quote: GP300_s65 was built south of GP13, covering an area of about 30 km²

station_count.note: The ICRC 2025 proceedings (arXiv:2507.05915) also report 65 detection units deployed by June 2025.
station_count.quote: the array was extended to its current 65-antenna stage, GP300_s65

summary.plain: A prototype radio antenna array in the Gobi Desert in China, testing the technology for a much bigger planned array to detect cosmic rays and neutrinos.
summary.technical: GRANDProto300 pathfinder array in the Gobi Desert near Dunhuang, China: grew from a 13-antenna stage (deployed 2023-06) to a 65-antenna stage covering ~30 km² (2025-04), validating the radio-detection approach for the full GRAND design.

technology.note: The quote is from the 2026 JINST paper (arXiv:2509.21306) and describes the technology; the 'Earth-skimming' wording found elsewhere is not in that paper.
technology.quote: large arrays of radio antennas that search for distinctive radio frequency signals emitted by extensive air showers ... radio-frequency signals that reach the array from near-horizontal directions, as expected from inclined air showers initiated by cosmic rays and neutrinos
technology.value: Radio antenna array detecting radio-frequency signals from inclined extensive air showers initiated by cosmic rays and neutrinos
